facts.claim: UNESCO element 'Kimjang, making and sharing kimchi in the Republic of Korea' is live and was inscribed in 2013 (8.COM) on the Representative List. Its text does not mention weddings; it mentions family methods 'typically transmitted from a mother-in-law to her newly married daughter-in-law'.
facts.quote: Inscribed in 2013 (8.COM) on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity ... typically transmitted from a mother-in-law to her newly married daughter-in-law.

facts.claim: UNESCO element 'Arirang, lyrical folk song in the Republic of Korea' is live and was inscribed in 2012 (7.COM). Its description text does not mention weddings; the page's keyword tags include 'Wedding' but the text never links Arirang to weddings, so it must not be presented as a wedding custom.
facts.quote: Inscribed in 2012 (7.COM) on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity ... Arirang is universally sung and enjoyed by the Korean nation.

facts.claim: Britannica: marriage is one of the most important passages in a Korean person's life, and hanbok is still commonly worn on special occasions including weddings, with different hanbok for weddings.
facts.quote: The most important passages in a person's life are the completion of a baby's first 100 days, one's marriage, and one's 61st birthday. ... even urban dwellers commonly still wear it on special occasions such as important family meetings, holidays, weddings, and funerals. ... There are different hanbok for special occasions, such as weddings

facts.claim: Smartraveller 'Getting married overseas' (last updated 18/08/2026): you can't register an overseas marriage in Australia, but in most cases it is legally recognised if valid under the law of the country where it happened and valid under Australian law had it occurred in Australia.
facts.quote: You can't register an overseas marriage in Australia. But in most cases, your marriage is legally recognised here. To be recognised, when you got married it must have been: valid under the law of the country where it happened; valid under Australian law if it had occurred in Australia.

facts.claim: Smartraveller 'Getting married overseas': some countries ask for proof you are free to marry, most commonly a CNI or registry certificates; ask the destination's embassy or consulate whether a CNI is needed, can be obtained in Australia, or needs an apostille; talk to a lawyer to confirm validity.
facts.quote: The most common documents you need are: a Certificate of No Impediment to Marriage (CNI); certificates from a registry of births, deaths and marriage. ... Contact your destination's embassy or consulate for specific details. ... Talk to a lawyer to confirm your overseas marriage certificate is valid in Australia.

facts.claim: Smartraveller CNI page (last updated 01/10/2026): DFAT issues CNIs through Australian Passport Offices, embassies and consulates overseas, and by mail; fees apply (no amounts recorded); at least one applicant must be an Australian citizen or permanent resident; ask whether the CNI must be issued in the country of marriage and whether it needs an apostille or authentication.
facts.quote: DFAT issues CNIs: through Australian Passport Offices across Australia; through Australian embassies, high commissions, and consulates overseas; by mail. ... Note that we charge fees for our service. ... At least one person applying for the CNI must be an Australian citizen or permanent resident.

facts.claim: Australian Embassy Seoul notarial page is live (title 'Notarial Services'). It issues a Certificate of No Impediment to Marriage (CNI), described as a general statement of Australian law; the CNI does not state the applicant is single (a Single Status Certificate comes from the Australian BDM registry).
facts.quote: A Certificate of No Impediement to Marriage (CNI) is a general statement of the law in Australia concerning the recognition of foreign marriages. ... The CNI does not states the applicant is currently single.

facts.claim: Embassy Seoul CNI requirements: originals only; applicant brings the completed CNI form (unsigned, signed before the consular officer), Australian passport, and divorce order or death certificate if applicable; partner brings foreign passport and the same if applicable; non-English documents need a professional translation.
facts.quote: Required documents for CNI (Original document only, copies not acceptable) ... Do not sign the last page as the consular officer will witness your signature on your appointment day.

facts.claim: Embassy Seoul: notarial services by appointment or by mail; fees apply for all services (card only; no amounts recorded); the embassy cannot witness signatures on documents for use in Korea, and consular staff cannot advise on specific legal requirements. No 'affidavit for marriage' service is listed; Australian affidavits are witnessed only for use in Australia.
facts.quote: Fees apply for all services. ... We are not able to witness signatures on documents that will be used in other countries. ... Consular staff cannot provide advice on specific legal requirements

facts.claim: Smartraveller South Korea (updated 12 October 2026, still current at 09 November 2026): overall advice 'Exercise normal safety precautions in South Korea'; no higher-level areas listed.
facts.quote: We advise: Exercise normal safety precautions in South Korea.

facts.claim: Smartraveller: the DMZ is mentioned under Regional threats (technically still at war; low-level clashes across the DMZ and Northern Limit Line; tensions can increase with little warning), with no separate advice level.
facts.quote: tensions can increase with little warning (as recorded in repo notes 02-research/pages/smartraveller.md)

facts.claim: Smartraveller weather: rainy/monsoon season usually June to August; typhoon season usually August to September; heatwaves between June and September; yellow dust and high pollution particularly March to May.
facts.quote: rainy/monsoon season 'usually from June to August'; typhoon season 'usually from August to September'; heatwaves 'between June and September'; yellow dust 'particularly from March to May'

facts.claim: Smartraveller entry (as at November 2026): Australian passport holders can visit as tourists for up to 90 days without a K-ETA; exempt from K-ETA until 31 December 2026; e-Arrival card within 3 days before arrival; conditions can change at short notice.
facts.quote: Australian passport holders can visit as tourists for stays of up to 90 days without applying for a K-ETA (or visa waiver). ... until 31 December 2026 ... Entry and exit conditions can change at short notice.

facts.claim: Smartraveller: same-sex relationships are not criminalised but are not legally recognised in South Korea.
facts.quote: Same-sex relationships and homosexuality are not criminalised, but same-sex relationships are not legally recognised.

facts.claim: Smartraveller: dual nationality recognised only in limited circumstances; male Australian-Korean dual nationals of military age may need to complete military service.
facts.quote: male Australian-Korean dual nationals of military age may need to complete military service (repo notes paraphrase of Smartraveller)

facts.claim: Smartraveller: public officials (including teachers, journalists and public servants) and their spouses cannot accept meals, gifts or other benefits above set limits (no amounts recorded). Relevant to chukuigeum only as a note for guests.
facts.quote: Public officials (including teachers, journalists, public servants) and spouses cannot accept meals, gifts or other benefits above set limits (repo notes)

facts.claim: Smartraveller: avoid demonstrations and large public gatherings, common in Seoul especially on weekends and public holidays; illegal to photograph military zones, assets, personnel and official buildings.
facts.quote: Avoid demonstrations and large public gatherings, common in Seoul, especially weekends and public holidays. ... illegal to photograph military zones, assets, personnel and official buildings (repo notes)

insider_details.detail: Order a CNI early: ask the district office in Korea whether it accepts an Australian-issued CNI or wants one from the Embassy in Seoul, and whether it needs an apostille, because the Embassy is appointment or mail only and apostilles take a few working days to collect.
A CNI is not proof of single status; if the district office asks for that, order a Single Status Certificate from your Australian state or territory registry before you fly.

For autumn dates, plan around typhoon season (usually August to September) and avoid the June to August monsoon for outdoor photos; spring brings yellow dust, so keep a covered option for hanbok portraits.
Australian guests can enter visa-free for up to 90 days and are K-ETA exempt only until 31 December 2026; for 2027 dates, recheck entry rules before invitations go out.
Brief guests not to photograph military sites or official buildings and to steer clear of weekend demonstrations in central Seoul when planning group outings.
